Hosts on Mobile — a Host Row in the Pull-Down Sheet

Features·seedling·proposed·JUL 12, 2026

On the touch layout kolu renders no host chrome at all — the chip row and add-host affordance are desktop-only — so on a phone you can't see, switch, or add hosts even though the host engine underneath is already layout-agnostic. This note proposes a host row inside the mobile pull-down sheet, mocked at phone width, reusing the desktop chip's exact pixel vocabulary.

Contents

The multi-host engine is done and it does not care what layout it’s in: the keyed padi host map, W9 retained switching (a switch repaints instantly from a kept surface), W10 persisted fleet (hosts survive a restart), and W5 per-host attention all live below the UI. But the only face that engine has is desktop. ChromeBar and its HostSelectorStrip are gated behind isDesktop(), and the touch layout — the pull-down sheet in packages/client/src/MobileChromeSheet.tsx — renders no host chrome whatsoever. So on a phone you cannot see which host you’re on, switch hosts, or add one. The capability exists; the surface doesn’t.

This note proposes that surface: a host row inside the mobile pull-down sheet. Everything below is mocked at phone width (≈390 px) so the design is something to look at, not read. The one hard constraint threads every mockup — the mobile chips are not a restyle.

Constraint — pixel-language identical to desktop

A mobile host chip is the same visual grammar as the desktop tab, not a lookalike. The connection dot tone comes from hostChipTone.dotClass (green only for connected, amber warming, red failed), the identity hue from hostHue, and the amber attention pill from ATTENTION_PILL_CLASS (the @kolu/solid-statepip token shipped in #1774, the Dock’s unread badge’s own source). A green dot, an amber 2, a violet chip must mean the same thing on a phone as on a laptop. Divergence isn’t a style choice — it’s a bug, because both surfaces read one token.

What a phone user gets

Pull the sheet down and a Hosts row sits at the top, above the existing palette / settings / inspector cluster. Each host is a chip carrying the desktop vocabulary verbatim: the connection dot, the local house glyph, the identity-hue border when active, and the amber attention pill when that host has agents awaiting you. A tap switches; the + adds.

Three hosts in the pull-down sheet. local is active — it wears its identity hue (slate) as a border + tinted belly, with a green dot and the house glyph. srid@zest shows a red dot: it’s failed, and you see that before switching, exactly as on desktop. prod carries an amber 2 — two agents awaiting you — in the same ATTENTION_PILL_CLASS pill the Dock uses. Every chip is a ≥44 px touch target.

Tap a chip — the canvas re-hues, instantly

A tap is one call: setActiveHost(host), the identical write the desktop strip makes. Because of W9, the target host’s surface is already retained, so the canvas repaints from it with no reload and no reconnect — the per-host hue wash on the canvas floor cross-fades to the new host, so switching feels like moving rooms, not reloading a page.The switch is a synchronous signal write — setActiveHost(props.host), and useEntry(activeHost) re-keys the per-host canvas. W9 (retained switching) means the surface for the target host is kept warm, so the repaint is immediate rather than a fresh attach. The mobile row calls the exact same function the desktop HostSelectorStrip does; there is no mobile-specific switch path.

Many hosts — the row scrolls sideways

When hosts outgrow the phone’s width the row becomes horizontally scrollable rather than wrapping or collapsing to a menu. A right-edge fade signals more chips off-screen; the active chip is what you scroll back to. This is the deliberately-simple mobile answer — desktop’s ⋯ +N overflow fold and sm..md dropdown collapse are width-measurement machinery a thumb-scroll makes unnecessary.Open design question, called out below: whether mobile should instead borrow the desktop overflow model (computeVisibleHosts + HostOverflowMenu). The prototype and these mockups assume the scroll-row; it’s the lighter build and reads naturally as a touch gesture, but it trades away the “active chip always visible without scrolling” guarantee the desktop fold keeps.

Adding a host on a phone

The desktop + opens AddHostAffordance — an anchored popover with an ALPHA notice, a docs link, and an ssh-target input. The prototype reused it verbatim, which surfaced the real design fork: that popover is anchored and fixed-width, so at phone width it overflows the viewport and clips. So this is presented as two mockups — the honest current behaviour, and a proposed mobile-native variant — for a design call.

Usable enough to demo, cramped enough that it shouldn’t ship as the mobile add surface. This is design input, not prototype scope — it was observed, not fixed.

Proposed — recommended. Instead of an anchored popover, the + expands an in-sheet section spanning the full sheet width: the same ALPHA notice and ssh field, but nothing to clip, a full-width 44 px input, and a thumb-sized Add button. It reuses the same client.hosts.add path — only the container changes from a portalled popover to a sheet section.

How it wires in

The whole point is that this is a thin leaf, not new machinery. App.tsx already forks on isDesktop(); the desktop branch mounts ChromeBar → HostSelectorStrip, and the touch branch mounts the pull-down sheet. This proposal adds one component — MobileHostRow — to that sheet, and it reads the exact same seams the desktop strip reads: padiMap.entries for the host list, each entry’s cells.urgency for the awaiting count, hostChipTone (dotClass / hostHue) for tone and identity, ATTENTION_PILL_CLASS for the pill, and setActiveHost for the switch.

No new electricity — this is not a receptacle

By the electricity test, MobileHostRow hides no hard volatility of its own: transport, reconnect, persistence, and retained-switch all live below it in the host map and the @kolu/surface-map layer. It is a presentation leaf that projects already-streamed state, the mobile twin of HostSelectorStrip. So it belongs in the client’s host/ module beside its desktop sibling — not a new @kolu/* package. The one shared thing worth watching is the vocabulary: hostChipTone and ATTENTION_PILL_CLASS are the single source both leaves must keep consuming, so the pixel-language constraint holds by construction rather than by discipline.

Implementation — one client-only PR

This is a single, client-only change threading existing seams — no server, no protocol, no package. It reuses one already-exported affordance (AddHostAffordance) and adds one component plus one mount line.

Piece What it is Grounding
MobileHostRow.tsx New leaf: the chip row + add affordance, ~130 lines reads padiMap.entries, entry.cells.urgency, calls setActiveHost
MobileChromeSheet.tsx One import + one mount line, host row above the control cluster packages/client/src/MobileChromeSheet.tsx
hostChipTone reuse dotClass / hostHue / hostLabel / sameHost / statusTitle packages/client/src/host/hostChipTone.ts
ATTENTION_PILL_CLASS reuse the amber pill token from #1774 @kolu/solid-statepip/pipVariant
add-host export existing AddHostAffordance, or build the in-sheet variant packages/client/src/host/HostSelectorStrip.tsx

Head start — a working prototype is already parked

A runnable prototype was built during the spike that produced this note and is parked on branch mobilereite (not merged, not PR’d): MobileHostRow.tsx, the MobileChromeSheet mount, and an export on AddHostAffordance. It was driven in a phone-emulated browser and confirmed the load-bearing behaviours — chips at exactly 44 px, overflow-x: auto scroll, a tap re-keying the canvas to the tapped host, and the add-popover overflow finding that drove the design fork above. The implementing agent can start from that commit rather than a blank file; the one real decision left is the add-host surface (reuse the cramped popover vs. build the in-sheet variant).

Decisions to settle before building

Two forks change the build and are srid’s call — they’re deliberately left open here because the whole note is a mockup to react to:

  • Add-host surface — reuse the current anchored AddHostAffordance popover (cheapest; visibly cramped at phone width), or build the proposed in-sheet full-width variant (a little more work; the honest mobile answer). Recommend the in-sheet variant.
  • Overflow model — the horizontally-scrolling row shown here (lighter, reads as a touch gesture), or port desktop’s ⋯ +N fold / dropdown collapse (keeps the active chip always visible without scrolling). Recommend the scroll-row.

One smaller choice is baked in as a default, not a question: the row lives at the top of the sheet, above the palette/settings cluster, because host identity is the most global thing in the sheet. Once srid reacts to these mockups, a /be run implements the chosen variants from the parked head-start.
